# Senāsanakkhandhaka (Kd 16)

**ID:** Kd 16
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Senāsanakkhandhaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The chapter on resting places

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (“The chapter on resting places” or “The Chapter on dwellings”) is the sixth chapter (CV VI) of the *Cullavagga* within the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Horner 1966; Norman 1983]. The text regulates monastic lodgings, detailing allowable types of buildings, methods for their construction and finishing, and permissible furnishings [SuttaCentral; Prebish 2002]. It lays down procedures for the appointment of monastic communal officers, notably the distributor of lodgings (*senāsanagāhāpaka*, Sanskrit: *śayyāsanagrāhaka*), an office instituted when the group of seventeen monks (*sattarasavaggiyā*) repaired a large monastery for the rains and were displaced by the group of six monks (*chabbaggiyā*) [Härtel 1956]. It also treats penal matters such as throwing a monk out of a communal dwelling or improperly disposing of heavy community property [Horner 1966]. Narratively, the chapter records the story of the merchant Anāthapiṇḍika, the donation of sixty dwellings to the universal community of the four quarters by a merchant of Rājagaha, and the *Tittira Jātaka* tale concerning precedence among the partridge, monkey, and elephant [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1982; Banerjee 1979].

Curated parallels to the text are found across the Vinayas of several early Buddhist schools, including the Sanskrit *Śayanāsanavastu* of the Mūlasarvāstivādins, its Tibetan and Chinese translations, as well as the corresponding chapters of the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka Vinayas [SuttaCentral; Härtel 1956; Banerjee 1979]. Portions of the chapter parallel individual discourses and narratives, including the *Sudattasutta* (SN 10.8; SA 592; SA2 186), the *Tittirajātaka* (Ja 37), and the *Hatthakasutta* (AN 3.35) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records widespread Pali-internal text reuse, especially with the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15), *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), and the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* (Kd 20), as well as substantial parallels identified in sub-commentarial texts such as the *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* and *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text cross-linguistically with the Sanskrit *Śayanāsanavastu*, *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and Tibetan *Vinayavastu* sections [DharmaNexus]. Modern English translations include that of Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
